blocks.text: 112 מוּסָף לְיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה 112
uncertainties: Left page number looks like '11' followed by a malformed or reversed '2' glyph (possible print artifact).
Header vowels are small and partly cut off at the top of the enlarged band, so they were read from the full scan.

blocks.text: וְאַתָּה אֱזוֹן קוֹל מְפָאֲרֶיךָ בְּכָל אֵבָרֵיהֶם. תֹּכֶן מִצְוֹות מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם בְּמָאתַיִם וְאַרְבָּעִים וּשְׁמֹנָה אֵבָרֵיהֶם: בְּזֶה חֹדֶשׁ תְּקוֹעַ שְׁלֹשִׁים. כְּמוֹ שְׁלֹשִׁים בְּכַף רַגְלֵיהֶם: שַׁי מוּסְפֵי יוֹם עֲשָׂרָה. כְּמוֹ עֲשָׂרָה בְּקַרְסֻלֵּיהֶם: גָּשִׁים פְּנֵי תֵבָה שַׁחֲרִית שְׁתַּיִם. כְּמוֹ שְׁתַּיִם בְּשׁוֹקֵיהֶם: רְשׁוּמִים קְרוֹת בּוֹ חֲמִשָּׁה. כְּמוֹ חֲמִשָּׁה עַל בִּרְכֵּיהֶם: דְּרוּשִׁים תְּקוֹעַ בַּכֶּסֶא בְּאֶחָד. כְּמוֹ אֶחָד בְּיַרְכוֹתֵיהֶם: קֶרֶן יִמְשְׁכוּ לְשַׁלֵּשׁ שְׁלֹשָׁה. כְּמוֹ שְׁלֹשָׁה בְּקוֹטָלֵיהֶם: הֵן מוּסְפֵי חֹדֶשׁ עַשְׁתֵּי עֶשְׂרֵה. כְּמוֹ עַשְׁתֵּי עֶשְׂרֵה צַלְעוֹתֵיהֶם: צָקוּן לַחֲשָׁם בְּרָכוֹת תֵּשַׁע. כְּמוֹ תִּשְׁעָה שֶׁבִּזְרוֹעוֹתֵיהֶם: וּמַלְכֻיּוֹת וְזִכְרוֹנוֹת וְשׁוֹפָרוֹת שְׁלֹשִׁים. כְּמוֹ שְׁלֹשִׁים בְּפִסַּת יְדֵיהֶם: פִּלּוּל תְּמִידִים שְׁמֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה. כְּמוֹ שְׁמֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה חוּלְיוֹת שֶׁבְּשִׁדְרוֹתֵיהֶם: זִבְחֵי תְמִידִים תְּקִיעוֹת תֵּשַׁע. כְּמוֹ תִּשְׁעָה שֶׁבְּרָאשֵׁיהֶם: עֲתִירוֹת שְׁתַּיִם שְׁחוֹחַ בָּם שְׁמֹנָה. כְּמוֹ שְׁמֹנָה שֶׁבְּצַוָּארֵיהֶם: חַק דָּתָם סְפָרִים חֲמִשָּׁה. כְּמוֹ חֲמִשָּׁה שֶׁבִּנְקָבֵיהֶם:
uncertainties: מִצְוֹות: there may be one vav or two (the alternative is מִצְוֹת). The holam dot above the vav is clear.
תְּקוֹעַ (it appears twice): the vowel under the tav could be a sheva or a hiriq (תִּקוֹעַ), and the dot on the vav could be a holam or a shuruk.
שְׁלֹשִׁים / שְׁלֹשָׁה: the holam on the lamed may be merged with the shin dot, so it could be a defective spelling without a holam.
מוּסְפֵי (it appears twice): there seems to be a rafe stroke over the pe.
בְּקַרְסֻלֵּיהֶם: there are crowded or extra marks under the qof and resh. The qubbutz under the samekh is likely but not certain.
יִמְשְׁכוּ: the vowel under the yod could be a hiriq or a patach.
שֶׁבְּשִׁדְרוֹתֵיהֶם: the vowel under the second shin could be a hiriq or a segol.
חַק: the mark under the het looks like a patach. A holam (חֹק) would be the expected reading, but it is not visible.
שֶׁבִּנְקָבֵיהֶם: the vowels on the bet and nun are small and hard to make out.
תְמִידִים after זִבְחֵי: I can't tell whether the tav has a dagesh.
This small superscript role mark sits mid-line before שָׂם. It looks most like ח׳ (chazzan), but ק׳ is possible.

blocks.text: שָׂם חֲלִיכוֹת עוֹלָם שִׁשָּׁה. כְּמוֹ שִׁשָּׁה בִּלְבָבֵיהֶם: טוּחוֹת וָכֶסֶל וְשֶׂכְוִי וְסַרְעַף וּבֶטֶן וָקֶרֶב וְעֶשְׁתּוֹנוֹתֵיהֶם. נֶפֶשׁ רוּחַ נְשָׁמָה יְחִידָה חַיָּה. עוֹר וּבָשָׂר וְגִיד וַעֲצָמוֹתֵיהֶם:
uncertainties: וְסַרְעַף: there is a mark above the final pe, possibly a rafe.
The last letter could be ח or ה. Read as ק(הל) ו(חזן).

blocks.text: יִשְׂאוּ עַֽיִן וְיַכְּרוּ אֹֽזֶן וְיִפְצוּ פֶּה וְלָשׁוֹן וְנִיב שִׂפְתוֹתֵיהֶם. מִכַּף רֶגֶל וְעַד רֹאשׁ נִתְוַכְּחוּ פְּרוּט מַֽעֲשֵׂיהֶם. כְּתִקֽוּעַ שׁוֹפָר בְּקוֹל יַחְפְּרוּ שׂוֹטְנֵיהֶם. לְהַֽצְדִּיקָם בְּיוֹם דִּין שְׁמֽוֹעַ שֵׁנִית מֵאֱלֹהֵיהֶם:
uncertainties: This stanza is set in a larger, different typeface. The short horizontal strokes under or before letters (עַֽיִן, אֹֽזֶן, מַֽעֲשֵׂיהֶם, כְּתִקֽוּעַ, לְהַֽצְדִּיקָם, שְׁמֽוֹעַ) are read as meteg, but some could be ink artifacts.
וְיַכְּרוּ: the vowel under the yod (patach or hiriq) and the dagesh in the kaf are unclear.
בְּקוֹל יַחְפְּרוּ: the words run together. A stroke between the lamed and the yod could be a meteg or a vav (which would give בְּקוֹלוֹ), and there is no clear word space.
שִׂפְתוֹתֵיהֶם: the hiriq under the shin and the sheva under the pe are likely but not certain.

blocks.text: Listen to the voice of those who glorify Thee with all their limbs, the number of whose commandments corresponds to their two hundred and fortyeight bones. On this New Moon they blow thirty blasts, like the thirty bones in the ball of their foot. The gift of homage of the Musaph sacrifice for the day numbers ten, like the ten bones in their ankles. They approach the Holy Ark twice in the morning, like the two bones in their thighs. Five are appointed to read the Torah on it, like the five bones in their knees. They are commanded to blow the Shofar on the first of the month, corresponding to the one bone in their hip. Three times do they sound long blasts on the horn, like the three bones of the hip-joint. The Musaph sacrifices of the New Moon are eleven in number, like their eleven ribs. Softly do they pour forth the prayer with the nine blessings, like the nine bones in their arm. There are thirty verses in Malkhuyoth, Zikhronoth and Shofaroth, like the thirty bones in their hand. The daily prayer consists of eighteen blessings, like the eighteen vertebrae in their spine. During the daily sacrifice they blow nine times, like the nine bones in their head. In the two prayers (morning and Musaph) they bow down eight times altogether like the eight bones in their neck. Their Torah is divided into five books, like the five organs of the senses in their cavities. The paths of the world (Mishnah) did He draw for them in six divisions, like the six divisions of the heart. Kidneys, loins, heart, brain, body, intestines with their sensations, soul, spirit, breath, personality, life-force, skin, flesh, sinews, and their bones.
uncertainties: 'fortyeight' is printed as one word without a hyphen.
'eigh-teen' and 'life-force' are broken across lines. 'eighteen' is joined here, and the hyphen in 'life-force' is kept.

blocks.text: They raise their eye, listen with the ear, open the mouth and speak; from the ball of the foot to the head every single action of theirs is examined when the Shofar is blown; at this sound their accusers blush, for they hear their justification for the second time on the day of judgment from their God.
uncertainties: 'justi-fication' is broken across lines and has been joined.
